subject.title: [Feature]: Add Antigravity CLI (agy) as CLI backend to replace deprecated google-gemini-cli

question: Should OpenClaw ship a first-party bundled Google Antigravity CLI route, and if so which single public provider/profile identity should replace the currently inconsistent `google-antigravity` and `google-antigravity-cli` proposals?
rationale: The source shows the capability is absent, while the open implementation introduces a compatibility-sensitive provider/auth/session contract that cannot be chosen safely from code evidence alone.

options.title: Sponsor a bundled Google plugin route
options.body: Adopt a single documented Antigravity CLI identity in the bundled Google plugin, preserve Gemini CLI separately, and require the linked PR to prove fresh setup and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Route it to an external plugin
options.body: Keep core unchanged and require a separately installed plugin to own `agy` discovery, setup, auth marker, documentation, and compatibility commitments.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bundled Google plugin route
recommendation.body: Adopt a single documented Antigravity CLI identity in the bundled Google plugin, preserve Gemini CLI separately, and require the linked PR to prove fresh setup and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Feature history connects this person to the relevant Google CLI and shared runtime/auth contract decisions.
